title: Skyfire: A Spectroscopic Census of Little Red Dots and Broad-Line AGN in the CEERS Field
comment: 20 Pages, 8 Figures, Submitted to ApJ
summary: We present the Skyfire program, a 21-hour Cycle 3 JWST/NIRSpec survey with the G395M medium-resolution grating covering five pointings in the Extended Groth Strip. The survey is designed to carry out a systematic census of faint, broad-line AGN candidates with a range of rest-optical colors identified at z > 3 by the Cosmic Evolution Early Release Science (CEERS) Survey. Our primary targets include photometrically-selected Little Red Dots (LRDs), blue extreme emission line galaxies (EELGs), and X-ray-detected AGN. We present spectroscopic redshifts for 178 sources observed by Skyfire, as well as a catalog of 34 sources with broad emission lines in the redshift range 2.7 < z < 6.5. Our broad-line sample includes 18 LRDs, which brings the spectroscopic completeness of LRDs with $β_{\rm opt}>-0.02$ in the CEERS field to 73%. We explore the prevalence of broad emission lines in photometrically-selected LRDs as a function of their rest-frame continuum slope and observed color distributions. We find the broad-line detection fraction in LRDs remains high at relatively blue rest-optical colors and extends smoothly into the bluer regime occupied by Little Blue Dots (LBDs). We discuss the implications of this finding for LRD-LBD unification scenarios. We also find that only 18% (3/17) of EELGs selected primarily for their high-equivalent-width emission lines and compact morphologies exhibit broad emission lines, suggesting these criteria alone are poor predictors of broad-line activity. We present a revised set of LRD selection criteria that captures bluer sources by extending down to $β_{\rm opt}=-0.52$. Using this new threshold, we find that $80.9^{+4.6}_{-7.5}\%$ of photometrically-selected LRDs brighter than 26.5 in F444W show broad emission lines and that LRDs make up 54% of the overall broad-line population identified in the CEERS field.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the Skyfire program, a 21-hour JWST/NIRSpec Cycle 3 survey with the G395M grating covering five pointings in the Extended Groth Strip. It provides spectroscopic redshifts for 178 sources and a catalog of 34 broad-line AGN candidates at 2.7 < z < 6.5. The survey finds that 80.9% of photometrically-selected Little Red Dots (LRDs) brighter than 26.5 in F444W show broad emission lines, and that LRDs constitute 54% of the broad-line population in the CEERS field. The authors also present revised LRD selection criteria extending to bluer rest-optical slopes (beta_opt = -0.52) and explore LRD-LBD unification and the poor predictive power of EELG criteria for broad-line activity.
AI.motivation: To systematically census faint, broad-line AGN candidates at z > 3, particularly photometrically-selected Little Red Dots, blue extreme emission line galaxies, and X-ray-detected AGN identified by the CEERS survey, in order to understand the spectroscopic nature and prevalence of broad-line activity in these populations.
AI.method: A 21-hour JWST/NIRSpec Cycle 3 survey using the G395M medium-resolution grating across five pointings in the Extended Groth Strip. It targets sources photometrically selected by CEERS including LRDs, EELGs, and X-ray-detected AGN. Spectroscopic redshifts and broad-line detections were obtained, with analyses of continuum slopes, observed colors, and revised selection criteria for LRDs.
AI.result: 178 sources obtained spectroscopic redshifts; 34 sources show broad emission lines at 2.7 < z < 6.5. The broad-line sample includes 18 LRDs, bringing the LRD spectroscopic completeness to 73%. Broad-line detection fraction in LRDs remains high at blue rest-optical colors, extending into LBD territory. Only 18% of EELGs show broad lines. Using a revised LRD criterion down to beta_opt = -0.52, 80.9% of LRDs brighter than 26.5 in F444W show broad emission lines, and LRDs constitute 54% of the broad-line population in the CEERS field.
AI.conclusion: Broad-line activity is ubiquitous among photometrically-selected LRDs, even at relatively blue rest-optical colors, supporting LRD-LBD unification. EELG selection criteria alone are poor predictors of broad-line activity. A revised, bluer LRD selection criterion is proposed that effectively captures a population that is predominantly composed of broad-line AGN.

title: Weighing Little Red Dots with Transient Events
comment: 11 pages, 6 figures, 1 table, submitted to the Astrophysical Journal (ApJ)
summary: Recent JWST observations have revealed a large population of compact red sources at $z \gtrsim 4$, known as Little Red Dots (LRDs), many of which show signatures of accreting massive black holes (BHs). The physical nature of these sources and their connection to host galaxies are under debate. We propose an independent avenue for constraining their nature through transient phenomena, such as tidal disruption events (TDEs) and quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs), arising from interactions between a star and the gas envelope surrounding the BH. These event rates depend sensitively on BH mass and provide a way to "weigh" LRDs. We calculate the expected TDE and QPE rates in LRDs under three distinct scenarios: (1) LRDs are truly overmassive BHs, (2) LRDs have BH masses following the classical local scaling relations (and the reported BH masses in observations are overestimated), and (3) the currently observed LRDs are only the tip of the iceberg of a larger population of low-mass BHs. We find that the predicted TDE and QPE rates differ dramatically across scenarios, especially in the presence of steep stellar cusps. The expected TDE rates per degree-square, assuming a Hernquist stellar distribution with a Bahcall-Wolf cusp embedded, are $2.78 \times 10^{-3}$, $1.96 \times 10^{-3}$, and $3.37 \times 10^{-2} \, {\rm yr}^{-1} \, {\rm deg}^{-2}$ for the three scenarios, respectively, while the QPE rates are $1.64 \times 10^{-2}$, $4.72 \times 10^{-2}$, and $4.96 \times 10^{-1} \, {\rm yr}^{-1} \, {\rm deg}^{-2}$. Upcoming wide-field surveys with Euclid, Roman, and LSST may be capable of detecting these high-redshift transient events and obtaining light curves, which encode additional information about the BH mass and the gas structure of LRDs. Stellar transient events will provide valuable insight into the early assembly of massive BHs.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using stellar transient phenomena—tidal disruption events (TDEs) and quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs)—as an independent method to constrain the nature of Little Red Dots (LRDs), the compact red sources at z≳4 observed by JWST that may host accreting massive black holes. By calculating expected TDE/QPE rates under three distinct scenarios for LRD BH masses, the authors find dramatically different predictions (e.g., TDE rates of 2.78×10⁻³ to 3.37×10⁻² yr⁻¹ deg⁻²), suggesting upcoming wide-field surveys (Euclid, Roman, LSST) could detect these events and discriminate between competing interpretations of LRD BH masses.
AI.motivation: The physical nature of Little Red Dots (LRDs)—compact red sources at z≳4 showing signatures of accreting massive black holes—and their relationship to host galaxies remains under debate. In particular, their reported BH masses are uncertain and may be overestimated. The paper aims to find an independent observational avenue to constrain LRD BH masses and thereby determine which population scenario is correct.
AI.method: The authors calculate expected TDE and QPE rates in LRDs under three scenarios: (1) LRDs host truly overmassive BHs, (2) LRDs follow classical local BH-host scaling relations (implying reported masses are overestimated), and (3) observed LRDs are only the bright tip of a much larger population of low-mass BHs. Rates are computed assuming a Hernquist stellar distribution with a Bahcall-Wolf cusp embedded, with event rates sensitive to BH mass and stellar structure.
AI.result: Predicted rates differ dramatically across scenarios. TDE rates per deg² are 2.78×10⁻³, 1.96×10⁻³, and 3.37×10⁻² yr⁻¹ deg⁻², while QPE rates are 1.64×10⁻², 4.72×10⁻², and 4.96×10⁻¹ yr⁻¹ deg⁻² for scenarios 1, 2, and 3, respectively—differences especially pronounced in the presence of steep stellar cusps.
AI.conclusion: Upcoming wide-field surveys including Euclid, Roman, and LSST may detect these high-redshift transient events and obtain light curves that encode information about BH mass and LRD gas structure. Stellar transient events thus offer valuable insight into the early assembly of massive black holes and can discriminate between competing models for LRD BH masses.

title: Reconciling Galactic rotation curve constraints with stellar stream modeling
comment: 12 pages (+ 2 pages in Appendix), 12 (+1) Figures, 2 (+1) Tables, accepted in Astronomy and Astrophysics, August 18th 2026. As a consequence, stellar streams are consistent with Galaxy masses ranging from 2.8 to 12.4 $10^{11}$ $M_{\odot}$
summary:
Recent Gaia-based measurements of the Milky Way rotation curve and stellar-stream modeling give significantly different estimates of the Galactic dynamical mass beyond Galactocentric radii of 15 kpc. The stream-based model predicts an outer halo five times more massive than that predicted by the Gaia rotation curve. We aim to test the impact of analytic assumptions used in stream modeling and to assess whether the currently available stream constraints can distinguish between low- and high-mass Galactic potentials. We first compared globular-cluster disruption in analytic and N-body Milky Way potentials. We then modeled Palomar~5 and ATLAS--Aliqa Uma, which are unique in probing the outer region beyond $R_{GC}$=15 kpc and are the most relevant to understanding the mass discrepancy. Both streams have usable constraints on sky position, proper motion, line-of-sight velocity, and RR~Lyrae distance. They were modeled for both a rotation-curve-based and a stream-based Galactic potential. In the N-body simulations, tidal shocks have a stronger effect on the closer orbit than on the more distant orbit, and therefore do not naturally explain the outer-Galaxy mass discrepancy. For the streams Palomar 5 and ATLAS--Aliqa Uma, simulations performed for both low- and high-mass Galactic potentials provide comparably good fits of their morphologies and kinematics. Neither potential provides a uniformly better match to all observables, and their differences are comparable to the present observational and modeling uncertainties.
  Current stream data do not discriminate between the low- and high-mass Milky Way models over the radial range probed by Palomar~5 and ATLAS--Aliqa Uma. This resolves the apparent tension between the rotation-curve- and stream-based constraints over this radial range.

AI.tldr: The paper tests whether stellar-stream modeling of Palomar 5 and ATLAS–Aliqa Uma can discriminate between low- and high-mass Galactic potentials, which differ by a factor of five in outer halo mass based on Gaia rotation curve vs. stream modeling estimates. Both potentials produce comparably good fits to observed stream morphologies and kinematics, and current stream data cannot distinguish between the two models, resolving the apparent mass discrepancy tension.
AI.motivation: Gaia-based rotation curve measurements and stellar-stream modeling give significantly different estimates of the Galactic dynamical mass beyond 15 kpc, with the stream-based model predicting a five times more massive outer halo. The authors aim to test whether analytic assumptions in stream modeling explain this discrepancy and whether current stream constraints can actually distinguish between low- and high-mass Galactic potentials.
AI.method: The authors (1) compared globular-cluster disruption in analytic and N-body Milky Way potentials to test for tidal-shock effects; and (2) modeled Palomar 5 and ATLAS–Aliqa Uma, two streams probing beyond R_GC=15 kpc, using constraints on sky position, proper motion, line-of-sight velocity, and RR Lyrae distances, for both a rotation-curve-based (low-mass) and a stream-based (high-mass) Galactic potential.
AI.result: N-body simulations show tidal shocks have a stronger effect on closer orbits than more distant ones, so they do not explain the outer-Galaxy mass discrepancy. For both Palomar 5 and ATLAS–Aliqa Uma, low- and high-mass Galactic potentials produce comparably good fits to morphology and kinematics; neither potential is uniformly better across all observables, with differences comparable to observational and modeling uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: Current stellar-stream data do not discriminate between low- and high-mass Milky Way models over the radial range probed by these streams. This resolves the apparent tension between rotation-curve- and stream-based mass constraints in this radial range.

title: Early Supermassive Black Holes and Little Red Dots Require Free-Fall Growth
comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, Submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics
summary: Supermassive black holes/active galactic nuclei (SMBHs/AGN), forming only a few hundred million years after the Big Bang as observed with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), challenge theoretical understanding. How could they grow so massive $(M_{\rm BH} > 10^6 {\rm \,M}_\odot)$ so quickly after initial seeding? Is this rapid growth related to the numerous and enigmatic Little Red Dots (LRDs), compact sources with AGN-like characteristics, discovered by JWST? To address these mysteries, we consider the first-order constraint on SMBH growth: enough baryonic material has to reach the vicinity of the SMBH seed, located near the bottom of the gravitational potential well of the host dark matter halo. We specifically examine cold-mode accretion, where gas from the cosmic environment flows into the virialized halo in cold streams without being shock-heated, efficiently reaching the center on a free-fall timescale. We find that cold mode accretion is necessary to supply material for the SMBHs to reach the observed masses, whereas for shock-heated gas inflow the required amount could only be supplied by implausibly rare halos. Moreover, cold-mode inflow in rare $(\sim1$ Gpc$^{-3}$) halos matches the mass and number of the massive quasars, and halos able to support super-Eddington accretion for massive SMBHs ($\sim10^7$ M$_\odot$) match LRD number densities. The decreasing LRD abundance at lower redshifts may then reflect the termination of cold-mode accretion in the growing host halos. The populations of massive SMBHs and LRDs at early times may thus arise naturally from cosmological structure formation, based on the abundance of halos capable of supplying sufficient material through cold accretion.

AI.tldr: This paper argues that cold-mode accretion—gas flowing into dark matter halos in cold streams without shock heating—is necessary to explain the rapid growth of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) observed by JWST at early cosmic times. The authors show that cold-mode inflow in rare halos can supply enough baryonic material to match the masses and number densities of massive quasars, while halos capable of supporting super-Eddington accretion match the populations of Little Red Dots (LRDs). The declining LRD abundance at lower redshifts is explained by the termination of cold-mode accretion as host halos grow.
AI.motivation: JWST observations reveal supermassive black holes/AGN forming only a few hundred million years after the Big Bang, with masses exceeding 10^6 solar masses, challenging theoretical models. The authors aim to address how such massive black holes could grow so quickly after initial seeding, and whether this is connected to the enigmatic Little Red Dots (LRDs)—compact AGN-like sources discovered by JWST.
AI.method: The authors apply a first-order constraint on SMBH growth: sufficient baryonic material must reach the vicinity of the seed black hole near the bottom of the host dark matter halo's gravitational potential well. They specifically examine cold-mode accretion, where gas flows into virialized halos via cold streams without shock heating, reaching the center on free-fall timescales. They compare this against shock-heated gas inflow scenarios and assess which halo populations can supply the required material.
AI.result: Cold-mode accretion is required to supply material for SMBHs to reach observed masses; shock-heated inflow would require implausibly rare halos. Cold-mode inflow in rare (~1 Gpc^-3) halos matches the mass and number density of massive quasars. Halos capable of supporting super-Eddington accretion for massive SMBHs (~10^7 solar masses) match LRD number densities. The decreasing LRD abundance at lower redshifts may reflect the end of cold-mode accretion in growing host halos.
AI.conclusion: The populations of massive SMBHs and LRDs at early times may arise naturally from cosmological structure formation, based on the abundance of halos capable of supplying sufficient material through cold-mode accretion. This framework connects observed SMBH and LRD populations to fundamental processes of gas accretion in early cosmic structure formation.

title: Sinking and spreading of metal pollution in magnetic white dwarfs
comment: submitted to MNRAS, comments welcome
summary: Observations of magnetic polluted white dwarfs indicate that most of them have higher concentrations of metals near the poles compared to lower latitudes. Maintaining such abundance gradients requires gravitational sinking times $t_\downarrow$ below the convection zone that are shorter than the horizontal spreading time $t_\leftrightarrow$ across the surface by convective eddies. We show analytically that $t_\downarrow/t_\leftrightarrow\propto T^{8/3}$, where $T$ is the temperature at the base of the convection zone, which rises by more than an order of magnitude as convection penetrates deeper into the atmosphere. Correspondingly, $t_\downarrow/t_\leftrightarrow$ jumps by several orders of magnitude, clearly delineating between hot white dwarfs with abundance variations and cold ones with homogenous surfaces. We incorporate magnetic fields self-consistently into the stellar structure and compute for the first time the sinking to spreading time-scale ratio as a function of $B$. Magnetic white dwarfs have shallower convection zones at a given $T_{\rm eff}$, and the inward penetration of convection shifts to lower $T_{\rm eff}$. Quantitatively, $B\sim 10^5\textrm{ G}$ extends the range for enhanced abundance patches from $T_{\rm eff}\gtrsim 30\,000 \textrm{ K}$ ($13\,000\textrm{ K}$) to $T_{\rm eff}\gtrsim 15\,000 \textrm{ K}$ ($6000\textrm{ K}$) for helium (hydrogen) dominated atmospheres, which is insufficient to explain the observed patchy white dwarfs, which are even colder. A possible solution is variability in the accretion rate on a time-scale of a decade, as recently detected in another white dwarf.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes why magnetic polluted white dwarfs exhibit metal abundance gradients (higher at poles than lower latitudes). The authors show analytically that the ratio of gravitational sinking time to horizontal convective spreading time scales as T^(8/3), making hot white dwarfs patchy and cold ones homogeneous. They incorporate magnetic fields into stellar structure for the first time to compute this time-scale ratio as a function of B, finding that magnetic fields extend the patchy surface regime to cooler temperatures but still insufficiently to explain observed patchy white dwarfs. They propose variable accretion rates over ~decade timescales as a possible resolution.
AI.motivation: Observations show magnetic polluted white dwarfs have higher metal concentrations near their poles than at lower latitudes. Maintaining these abundance gradients requires that gravitational settling below the convection zone is faster than horizontal spreading by convective eddies. The authors aim to understand the physical conditions under which such abundance patches can persist and whether magnetic fields can extend this regime.
AI.method: Analytical derivation showing t_down/t_spread ∝ T^(8/3) at the base of the convection zone. The authors incorporate magnetic fields self-consistently into the stellar structure models and compute, for the first time, the sinking-to-spreading time-scale ratio as a function of magnetic field strength B.
AI.result: The time-scale ratio jumps by several orders of magnitude with effective temperature, clearly separating hot white dwarfs (with abundance variations) from cold ones (homogeneous surfaces). Magnetic white dwarfs have shallower convection zones at a given Teff, and the inward penetration of convection shifts to lower Teff. B~10^5 G extends the patchy-abundance regime from Teff≳30,000 K (13,000 K) to Teff≳15,000 K (6,000 K) for helium (hydrogen) atmospheres, but this remains insufficient to explain colder observed patchy white dwarfs.
AI.conclusion: Magnetic fields alone cannot fully explain the observed cold patchy magnetic white dwarfs. The authors suggest that variability in accretion rate on a timescale of about a decade—as recently observed in another white dwarf—may resolve the discrepancy between theory and observations.

title: ACES VII. Compact Continuum Source Catalog of the Central Molecular Zone
comment: 25 pages, 11 figures, accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal
summary: The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) resides in the inner few hundred parsecs of our Galaxy, and despite being the largest reservoir of dense molecular gas in the Milky Way, it has a relatively low present-day star formation rate (SFR) of $\sim0.08~M_{\odot}~\text{yr}^{-1}$. Continuum and spectral line observations from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) CMZ Exploration Survey (ACES) provide the first full-coverage, high-resolution map of the inner 200 parsecs of the CMZ at 3 mm. In this paper we present the ACES catalog of compact continuum sources, the most complete catalog of potential sites of star formation in the CMZ to date. Using an automated dendrogram-based source extraction procedure in combination with a by-eye morphological classification scheme, we produce a `full' catalog of 1735 detections in total. Additionally, we use spectral index measurements to generate a `filtered' catalog of 567 sources with minimal contamination from non-thermal filaments and extended free-free emission. We find that 359 ($\sim63\%$) of the filtered catalog sources are located at column densities $< 10^{23}$ cm$^{-2}$, outside of the densest molecular cloud regions, 195 of which have not been identified in previous surveys. After cross-referencing with various catalogs generated from data at different wavelengths, we consider it likely that many of these newly discovered detections are produced by pre/protostellar sources or compact HII regions.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the ACES catalog of compact continuum sources in the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ), the most complete catalog of potential star-forming sites in the Galaxy's inner 200 parsecs to date. Using ALMA 3mm data with dendrogram-based extraction and morphological classification, it produces a full catalog of 1735 detections and a filtered catalog of 567 sources cleaned of contamination, finding 359 sources at column densities below 10^23 cm^-2, many newly discovered and likely tracing pre/protostellar sources or compact HII regions.
AI.motivation: The CMZ contains the largest reservoir of dense molecular gas in the Milky Way yet has a surprisingly low star formation rate. A complete, high-resolution catalog of potential star-forming sites is needed to understand the mechanisms suppressing star formation in this extreme environment.
AI.method: The study uses ALMA CMZ Exploration Survey (ACES) 3mm continuum and spectral line data covering the inner 200 parsecs. An automated dendrogram-based source extraction algorithm is combined with by-eye morphological classification, and spectral index measurements are used to filter out contamination from non-thermal filaments and extended free-free emission.
AI.result: The analysis yields a full catalog of 1735 compact continuum sources and a filtered catalog of 567 sources with minimal contamination. Of these, 359 (~63%) lie below column densities of 10^23 cm^-2 outside the densest clouds, with 195 being new detections not seen in previous surveys. Cross-referencing suggests many are likely pre/protostellar sources or compact HII regions.
AI.conclusion: The ACES catalog provides the most complete census of potential star formation sites in the CMZ to date. The discovery of many new sources outside the densest regions suggests that star formation tracers may be more widespread than previously recognized, offering new constraints on the low star formation efficiency of the CMZ.

title: Exploring stellar evolution with Luminous Red Novae and Interacting Gap Transients
comment: Submitted for review as Proceedings of IAU Symposium No. 405 (Editors: Hanin Kuncarayakti, Tuomas Kangas, Melina Bersten)
summary: Interacting gap transients encompass several families of astrophysical phenomena where eruptive mass loss and interaction play an important role in shaping the observational properties and energetics of the events. Composed of Luminous Red Novae (LRNe), Intermediate Luminosity Red Transients (ILRTs), Luminous Blue Variable (LBV) giant eruptions, and pre-supernova precursors, interacting gap transients offer crucial insights into unstable mass transfer, extreme stellar mass loss, and binary evolution. In these proceedings, I review the observational signatures, progenitors, physical origin, and classification challenges of these heterogeneous phenomena. Finally, I highlight how ongoing and future wide-field time-domain missions will revolutionize this field by compiling complete volume-limited samples, tracking faint pre-outburst precursors, and establishing statistical links between gap transient families and their progenitor populations.

AI.tldr: A review of interacting gap transients (LRNe, ILRTs, LBV giant eruptions, pre-supernova precursors), covering their observational signatures, progenitors, physical origins, and classification challenges, with an outlook on how future time-domain surveys will enable complete samples and statistical population studies.
AI.motivation: Interacting gap transients are heterogeneous astrophysical phenomena bridging eruptive mass loss and interaction-driven events, yet they remain poorly understood and difficult to classify. A consolidated review is needed to synthesize current knowledge and identify how upcoming surveys will advance the field.
AI.method: A proceedings-style review paper that synthesizes observational data and theoretical understanding of four families—LRNe, ILRTs, LBV giant eruptions, and pre-supernova precursors—examining their observational signatures, progenitor systems, physical origin mechanisms, and classification frameworks, while projecting the impact of future wide-field time-domain surveys.
AI.result: The paper summarizes current understanding of these transient families and highlights that ongoing/future wide-field time-domain missions will enable complete volume-limited samples, detection of faint pre-outburst precursors, and statistical establishment of links between gap transient classes and their progenitor populations.
AI.conclusion: Interacting gap transients provide critical insights into unstable mass transfer, extreme stellar mass loss, and binary evolution; future time-domain surveys will be transformative in resolving classification ambiguities and establishing population-level statistical connections.

title: The Halo Gas of Local Spiral Galaxies and the Link to Gaseous Satellites
comment: Submitted to The Astrophysical Journal. Comments are welcome
summary: Gaseous satellites orbiting massive host galaxies experience gas stripping and may contribute additional gas to the hosts' circumgalactic medium (CGM). We identify a sample of 21 local spiral galaxies ($<$15 Mpc) and characterize their gaseous satellite populations from existing HI surveys to investigate the connection between host galaxy CGM and satellite gas content. Most of our spiral hosts have $\leq3$ gaseous satellites in their halos with $M_{\rm HI}\gtrsim10^{7}~M_\odot$. Using 26 HST/COS QSO sightlines at impact parameters of 0.1--0.9 $R_{\rm 200c}$, we find that the CGM of $z\sim0$ spiral galaxies show large intrinsic scatters ($\sim1-2$ dex) in ion column densities and harbor a total cool gas mass of $2.5^{+7.5}_{\rm -1.9}\times10^9~(0.3Z_\odot/Z')~M_\odot$, largely consistent with their $z\sim0.2$ counterparts (e.g., COS-Halos). Splitting our sample by the presence of gaseous satellites, we find that galaxy hosts with gaseous satellites have higher detection rates (up to 50\%) in metal ion absorbers, including OI, AlII, CII, SiII, SiIII, and SiIV, possibly because their CGM is more metal enriched or has more ionized gas in the cool phase. However, the CGM column densities show no significant correlation with either the number of gaseous satellites or their total HI masses, suggesting that the contribution from the gaseous satellites to the host CGM is likely small compared to the intrinsic scatters in the CGM profiles, and the profile trends are mainly influenced by sightlines' proximity to the hosts. The CGM detection rate becomes elevated when a sightline is within half the virial radius of a massive gaseous satellite (LMC-like or higher mass), likely due to stripped debris.

AI.tldr: This study of 21 local spiral galaxies identifies their gaseous satellite populations and investigates the connection between host galaxy CGM and satellite gas content using HI surveys and 26 HST/COS QSO sightlines. They find that satellites contribute little to the host CGM column density trends (dominated by intrinsic scatter), though hosts with satellites show higher metal-ion detection rates, and sightlines passing near massive gaseous satellites show elevated CGM detections likely from stripped debris.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether gaseous satellites undergoing ram-pressure stripping contribute detectable gas to the circumgalactic medium (CGM) of massive host galaxies, and to understand the connection between satellite gas content and host CGM properties.
AI.method: Identify 21 local spiral galaxies (<15 Mpc) and characterize their gaseous satellite populations from HI surveys. Use 26 HST/COS QSO sightlines at impact parameters of 0.1-0.9 R_200c to probe the CGM. Split host sample by presence/absence of gaseous satellites and compare metal-ion absorption detection rates, column densities, and correlation with satellite number/mass.
AI.result: Most spiral hosts have ≤3 gaseous satellites with M_HI≥10^7 Msun. The z~0 spiral CGM shows ~1-2 dex intrinsic scatter in ion column densities and total cool gas mass of 2.5^{+7.5}_{-1.9}×10^9 Msun, consistent with z~0.2 counterparts. Hosts with gaseous satellites show higher detection rates (up to 50%) in metal ion absorbers (OI, AlII, CII, SiII, SiIII, SiIV), but CGM column densities show no significant correlation with satellite number or total HI mass. Detection rates elevate when a sightline passes within half the virial radius of a massive (LMC-like or higher) satellite.
AI.conclusion: Gaseous satellite contributions to the host CGM are likely small compared to intrinsic scatter in CGM profiles, with profile trends mainly driven by sightline proximity to hosts. However, stripped debris from massive gaseous satellites can locally enhance CGM metal-ion detection rates along nearby sightlines.

title: Modeling Rotation in the Old, Cold Domain: Implications on Gyrochronology and the Stellar Magnetic Wind
comment: 21 Pages, 14 figures, submitted to AAS journals
summary: Gyrochronology ties stellar rotation periods to ages. It is well studied in the young, open cluster age domain, but there are few constraints on gyrochronology in the old field star regime. In this work we use gyro-kinematic ages to explore the spin down of stars in this formerly inaccessible domain. Using forward modeling techniques which relax strict Rossby scaled assumptions, we find evidence for a departure from a standard spin down models. This departure can be explained with a mass-dependent term either in the global strength of the stellar wind or in the relationship between angular velocity and wind strength. Models with this additional mass- dependence help explain prior difficulty in fitting open cluster rotation distributions across the full mass range. Additionally, we use rotation models to identify an mass-dependent age domain over which wind driven stellar spin down can be isolated from other physical effects. For lower mass stars, this age domain is most affected by the core-envelope coupling timescale, where as higher mass stars are more subject to inertial effects late in their main sequence lifetimes. Using simple, analytic models of stellar spin down in this domain is unable to determine whether the stellar wind has a mass-dependence or if the stellar wind is strictly Skumanich-like in nature. In future studies of rotational and dynamo evolution we advocate for a forward modeling approach to gyrochronology over purely empirical approaches due to its superior ability to trace physical effects governing stellar spin down.

AI.tldr: This paper uses gyro-kinematic ages and forward modeling to explore stellar spin-down in the poorly constrained old field star regime, finding evidence for a mass-dependent departure from standard spin-down models, and advocating for forward modeling over purely empirical gyrochronology approaches.
AI.motivation: Gyrochronology (tying stellar rotation periods to ages) is well-studied for young open clusters but lacks constraints in the old field star regime, leaving a critical gap in understanding stellar spin-down over long timescales.
AI.method: The authors employ forward modeling techniques that relax strict Rossby-scaled assumptions, using gyro-kinematic ages to explore spin-down of old field stars. They also use rotation models to identify a mass-dependent age domain where wind-driven spin-down can be isolated from other effects, and compare against simple analytic spin-down models.
AI.result: Evidence for a departure from standard spin-down models is found, explicable by a mass-dependent term in either global stellar wind strength or the angular velocity-wind strength relationship. The analysis shows that for lower-mass stars, core-envelope coupling timescale dominates the relevant age domain, while higher-mass stars are more affected by inertial effects late in their main-sequence lifetimes. Simple analytic models cannot distinguish between mass-dependent winds and strictly Skumanich-like winds.
AI.conclusion: A mass-dependent modification to standard spin-down laws helps resolve prior difficulties fitting open cluster rotation distributions. The authors advocate for forward modeling approaches to gyrochronology over purely empirical methods due to their superior ability to trace the physical mechanisms governing stellar spin-down.

title: Local Heavily Obscured Active Galaxies Observed With Chandra (I): Spectral Properties of the Nuclear and Extended X-ray Emission
comment: accepted in ApJ, 62 pages, 31 figures
summary: The Chandra X-ray Observatory has revealed that kiloparsec-scale extended X-ray emission is commonly associated with heavily absorbed ($\log (N_{H}$/cm$^{-2})\,>\, 23$) Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) in the local Universe. We present a homogeneous spatially resolved spectral analysis of a sample of nearby obscured AGN observed with deep ($>100$~ks) Chandra/ACIS exposures and all associated with extra-nuclear extended emission. Exploiting the sub-arcsecond resolution of Chandra, we separate unresolved nuclear emission from physically distinct extended regions and model their spectra using photoionized and thermal plasma components. The extended emission is spectrally complex, requiring a combination of photoionized and collisionally ionized components in most regions. The spectral parameters exhibit systematic radial variations, with nuclear regions typically hosting higher-column and higher-ionization components, while extended regions span similarly broad but overlapping ranges without a simple monotonic radial progression. Hard ($>3$ keV) X-ray emission in excess of nuclear PSF spillover is detected in 19/20 sources, while extended Fe~K$α$ emission is observed in 12/20 systems. These results establish a uniform baseline for the X-ray properties of heavily obscured AGN and provide constraints on the geometry and physical conditions of AGN-driven feedback in the local Universe.

AI.motivation: To establish a uniform observational baseline for the X-ray properties of heavily obscured AGN and constrain the geometry and physical conditions of AGN-driven feedback in the local Universe, given that kiloparsec-scale extended X-ray emission is commonly associated with such obscured AGN but was previously lacking homogeneous systematic characterization.
AI.method: Spatially resolved spectral analysis of 20 nearby obscured AGN (log N_H > 23) using deep (>100 ks) Chandra/ACIS observations. title: Conspicuous Gas, Cryptic Dust: Spectroscopy and Chromaticity of Complex Periodic Variables
comment: Submitted to AAS Journals
summary: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young low-mass stars whose light curves show periodic dips indicative of transiting corotating material. The origin and composition of this material are unclear. Here we present new optical and near-infrared spectroscopy and photometry of four CPVs from Magellan, Keck, Hale, MuSCAT1, MuSCAT2, Tierras, KeplerCam, and TESS. The spectra imply that CPVs host magnetically bound circumstellar plasma clumps, on the basis of sinusoidal-in-time Balmer emission out of transit, and Balmer dimming during transit. Yet large night-to-night changes in circumstellar hydrogen emissivity occur without clear changes in light curve morphology, suggesting that the sharp flux dips are caused not by circumstellar plasma but by dust. Optical chromaticities (depth proportional to $λ^{-β}$, with $β$ = 0.79 $\pm$ 0.16) support this, but the power law breaks in the near-infrared, where a single power law under-predicts the depths observed at 2.1 microns. We therefore favor dips caused by dusty plasma clumps with opaque cores and optically thin halos, though we cannot rule out models in which the dust properties vary per-star or per-epoch. Observations at wavelengths greater than 2 microns and less than 0.4 microns would test this interpretation and clarify the dust's origin.

The spectra reveal magnetically bound circumstellar plasma clumps, while light curve analysis suggests flux dips are caused by dusty plasma clumps with opaque cores and optically thin halos rather than plasma alone.
AI.motivation: CPVs are young low-mass stars with periodic light-curve dips indicating transiting corotating material, but the origin and composition of this material are poorly understood.
AI.method: The authors obtained optical and near-infrared spectroscopy and photometry of four CPVs using observations from Magellan, Keck, Hale, MuSCAT1, MuSCAT2, Tierras, KeplerCam, and TESS. They analyzed Balmer emission variations and chromaticity of dip depths across wavelengths.

title: The gradual decline of Ly$α$ visibility in the CANDELS fields: evidence for the combined effects of galaxy evolution and reionization
comment: 18 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to the A&A journal. Comments are welcome
summary: We investigate the evolution of Ly$α$ visibility and the physical properties of Ly$α$ emitters (LAEs) across the five CANDELS fields using publicly available JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectroscopy. Our catalog comprises 3446 spectroscopically confirmed sources at 4 $\leq $ z < 14.2, including 3361 star-forming galaxies (SFGs), of which 539 are robust (S/N > 3) LAEs. We measure the fraction of LAEs with EW$_0$ > 25A (X$_{\mathrm{Lyα}}$) and trace its redshift evolution in two UV luminosity bins, namely -20.25 < M$_{\mathrm{UV}}$ < -18.75 and -21.75 < M$_{\mathrm{UV}}$ < -20.25. Within the fainter-UV range, X$_{\mathrm{Lyα}}$ increases from z = 5 to z = 6 at 3$σ$ significance and subsequently declines toward higher redshifts with a significant monotonic trend at z > 6. We also investigate the physical properties of both LAEs and the full SFG population. We find that the stellar mass, UV slope $β$, stellar reddening, SFR, metallicity, sSFR, and burstiness of LAEs remain approximately stable with redshift. The only exception is the mass-weighted age which decreases with increased redshift. Conversely, the properties of the full SFG population evolve significantly, progressively approaching the region of galaxy-property space occupied by LAEs as redshift increases. This suggests that galaxy evolution may enhance the intrinsic production and escape of Ly$α$ photons toward earlier epochs. We argue that this effect should be accounted when inferring the evolution of the neutral hydrogen content of the IGM from the observed visibility of Ly$α$ emission. To this end, we employ a physically motivated framework based on the Attenuation-Free Model, jointly accounting for galaxy evolution and IGM attenuation. Our observations favor reionization histories that proceed gradually over scenarios characterized by a rapid increase in the cosmic neutral hydrogen fraction.

The LAE fraction (X_Lyα) increases from z=5 to z=6 in the fainter UV bin, then declines monotonically toward higher redshifts. While LAE physical properties remain stable with redshift, the full star-forming galaxy population evolves to increasingly resemble LAEs toward earlier epochs, suggesting galaxy evolution enhances Lyα production/escape. Using a physically motivated Attenuation-Free Model framework that jointly accounts for galaxy evolution and IGM attenuation, the observations favor gradual reionization over scenarios with rapid neutral hydrogen increases.

AI.method: JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectroscopy across five CANDELS fields is used to construct a catalog of 3446 spectroscopically confirmed sources (4≤z<14.2). LAE fractions are measured in two UV luminosity bins and traced as a function of redshift. Physical properties (stellar mass, UV slope, reddening, SFR, metallicity, sSFR, burstiness, mass-weighted age) of LAEs and the full SFG population are compared. LAE physical properties remain approximately constant with redshift except mass-weighted age, which decreases with increasing redshift. AI.conclusion: Galaxy evolution significantly influences the intrinsic Lyα visibility and must be accounted for when inferring IGM neutral hydrogen content from Lyα observations. The observed data support a gradual reionization scenario once intrinsic galaxy evolution effects are jointly modeled.

title: A Probabilistic Framework for Incorporating Helioseismic Far-Side Active Regions into SFT Models
comment: 16 Pages, 8 Figures, Accepted for Publication in ApJS
summary: Surface Flux Transport (SFT) models are routinely used to model the Sun's photospheric magnetic field and provide inner boundary conditions for coronal and heliospheric models, yet they remain fundamentally limited by the lack of direct information about flux emergence on the far side of the Sun. To address this, we develop a framework for incorporating helioseismic images of far-side active regions (HIFAR), into the Advective Flux Transport (AFT) model. Using near-simultaneous magnetic flux maps (HIFARM) inferred from HIFAR, and STEREO/EUVI 304 A observations from 2010 May 13 to 2014 August 18, we develop a logistic regression model to estimate the probability that a helioseismic detection corresponds to an AR based on descriptors of magnetic flux, field strength, and location. The model achieves a precision of 0.93 for active region (AR) detections at a probability threshold of 0.73, selected to reject 90% of "ghost" ARs. We also derive an empirical scaling relationship between HIFARM and AFT flux to place HIFARM on the AFT flux scale and demonstrate that the framework reproduces the flux evolution of ARs consistent with near-side observations over multiple solar rotations. At the global scale, we find that conventional near-side-driven AFT simulations underestimate the total unsigned magnetic flux by ~10-20% of the Sun's total magnetic flux budget. The probabilistic AR detection model and the complete framework developed in this work provide a practical pathway for incorporating helioseismic far-side ARs into SFT models, a step toward realistic modeling of full-Sun magnetic field.

AI.method: The authors incorporate Helioseismic Images of Far-side Active Regions (HIFAR) into the AFT model. Using near-simultaneous magnetic flux maps (HIFARM) from HIFAR and STEREO/EUVI 304 A observations (2010-2014), they: (1) develop a logistic regression model estimating the probability that a helioseismic detection corresponds to an AR based on flux, field strength, and location descriptors; and (2) derive an empirical scaling relationship between HIFARM and AFT flux to calibrate HIFARM onto the AFT flux scale.

The framework reproduces AR flux evolution consistent with near-side observations over multiple solar rotations. At the global scale, conventional near-side-driven AFT simulations underestimate total unsigned magnetic flux by ~10-20% of the Sun's total magnetic flux budget.
AI.conclusion: The probabilistic AR detection model and the complete framework provide a practical pathway for incorporating helioseismic far-side ARs into SFT models, representing a step toward realistic full-Sun magnetic field modeling.

title: Accretion-disk sizes in two quasars with interferometrically resolved broad-line regions at $z=2.3$ and $z=4.0$
comment: 11 pages, 7 figures, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: We present the first direct comparison between accretion-disk (AD) and broad-line region (BLR) sizes in quasars at z > 2, combining continuum reverberation mapping with interferometric BLR constraints from GRAVITY and GRAVITY+. Using medium-band photometric monitoring with the MPG/ESO 2.2 m telescope, we measure inter-band continuum lags in SDSS J092034.17+065718.0 at z = 2.33 (J0920) and SMSS J052915.80-435152.0 at z = 3.96 (J0529), among the most luminous quasars known (Lbol ~ 10^48 erg s^-1). These are currently the only two quasars at z > 2 with spatially resolved BLRs and dynamical black-hole masses from interferometry. We detect significant continuum lags in both quasars, increasing monotonically with wavelength. The inferred UV disk sizes are RAD = 4.35 +0.78/-0.91 light-days for J0529 and RAD = 3.15 +0.50/-0.48 light-days for J0920. For J0920, accreting at lambda_Edd ~ 7-20, the disk size is consistent with standard thin-disk expectations despite its super-Eddington regime. For J0529, the disk size agrees with thin-disk predictions using the single-epoch black-hole mass, but implies disk inflation by a factor of a few if the GRAVITY+ dynamical mass, an order of magnitude lower, is adopted. UV continuum disk sizes therefore provide an independent physical scale constraining black-hole mass and accretion-rate models, particularly where BLR kinematics are dominated by outflows. The interferometric BLR sizes reveal pronounced radial hierarchies, with RBLR/RAD ~ 270 for J0529 (Hbeta) and ~115 for J0920 (Halpha). The successful lag detections at Lbol ~ 10^48 erg s^-1 show that continuum reverberation mapping remains feasible for the most luminous systems, opening a path to larger samples with surveys such as the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's LSST.

Significant wavelength-dependent continuum lags were detected, yielding UV disk sizes of ~3-4 light-days. While disk sizes agree with thin-disk predictions under single-epoch BH masses, adopting the lower dynamical mass for J0529 implies disk inflation. Interferometric BLR sizes show large radial hierarchies (R_BLR/R_AD ~115-270). The success demonstrates that continuum reverberation mapping works at the highest quasar luminosities, enabling larger future samples via LSST.
AI.motivation: To directly compare accretion-disk and broad-line region physical scales in the most luminous high-redshift (z>2) quasars, where BLR kinematics may be outflow-dominated, in order to constrain black-hole mass and accretion-rate models using an independent physical scale.
AI.method: Combined continuum reverberation mapping using medium-band photometric monitoring with the MPG/ESO 2.2 m telescope (to measure inter-band continuum lags) with interferometric BLR size measurements and dynamical black-hole masses from GRAVITY and GRAVITY+. Applied to two ultraluminous quasars (J0920 at z=2.33, J0529 at z=3.96) with Lbol ~ 10^48 erg/s.

UV disk sizes: R_AD = 4.35 +0.78/-0.91 light-days (J0529) and 3.15 +0.50/-0.48 light-days (J0920). J0920's disk is consistent with thin-disk predictions despite super-Eddington accretion (lambda_Edd ~ 7-20). J0529's disk matches thin-disk expectations with single-epoch mass but implies inflation by a few if the lower dynamical mass is used. Interferometric BLR sizes give R_BLR/R_AD ~270 (J0529, Hbeta) and ~115 (J0920, Halpha).
AI.conclusion: Reverberation mapping of continuum emission is feasible at the highest quasar luminosities (Lbol ~ 10^48 erg/s), and UV disk sizes serve as an independent physical scale to test black-hole mass and accretion models, especially where BLR kinematics are outflow-dominated. This paves the way for significantly larger samples using upcoming surveys such as LSST.

title: Discovery and Characterization of Three New High-amplitude delta Scuti Stars from TESS Observations
comment: 20 pages, 10 figures, 6 tables. Published in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: We report the discovery and detailed analysis of three new high-amplitude δ Scuti (HADS) stars, TIC 408074920, TIC 189714989, and TIC 34137913, identified from Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite short-cadence observations. Fourier analysis reveals dominant radial modes accompanied by rich harmonic structures in all three stars, confirming their HADS classification. In addition, TIC 189714989 exhibits clear symmetric side peaks around the radial harmonics, indicative of amplitude and/or phase modulation. Broadband spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting constrained by Gaia DR3 parallaxes provides independent estimates of the stellar effective temperatures and radii. These are compared with results from stellar evolutionary and seismic modeling based on MESA and GYRE. For two targets, the SED-derived and seismic radii are mutually consistent, while TIC 408074920 displays a significant discrepancy, plausibly attributable to the different sensitivities of the two methods and additional systematic effects. These findings highlight the diversity of amplitude variability among classical HADS and emphasize the importance of the long-term monitoring that future missions such as PLATO will allow in order to explore the underlying physical mechanisms of this variability.

AI.tldr: The paper reports the discovery and analysis of three new high-amplitude δ Scuti (HADS) stars from TESS short-cadence data, confirming their classification via dominant radial modes with harmonic structures, detecting amplitude/phase modulation in one target, and comparing SED-based and seismic stellar parameters. Two stars show consistent radii between methods, while one shows a discrepancy, highlighting diversity in HADS variability and motivating long-term monitoring by future missions.
AI.motivation: To expand the known census of high-amplitude δ Scuti stars and investigate their pulsational characteristics, amplitude variability, and to cross-validate independent stellar parameter estimation methods (SED fitting vs. seismic modeling).
AI.method: Fourier analysis of TESS short-cadence photometry; broadband SED fitting constrained by Gaia DR3 parallaxes for effective temperatures and radii; stellar evolutionary and seismic modeling using MESA and GYRE; comparison of SED-derived and seismic radii.
AI.result: All three stars are confirmed as HADS with dominant radial modes and rich harmonic structures. TIC 189714989 shows symmetric side peaks around radial harmonics indicating amplitude and/or phase modulation. SED-derived and seismic radii agree for two targets but disagree significantly for TIC 408074920.
AI.conclusion: The findings reveal diversity in amplitude variability among classical HADS and underscore the need for long-term monitoring (e.g., via PLATO) to understand the underlying physical mechanisms of this variability.

title: ELVES-Dwarf. II. A Systematic Search for Satellite Systems of Dwarf Galaxies in the Local Volume
comment: Submitted to ApJ. Data available on the survey website: https://elves-surveys.github.io/elves-dwarf/
summary: We present the Exploration of Local VolumE Satellites of Dwarf Galaxies (ELVES-Dwarf) survey, a systematic census of satellite systems around dwarf hosts in the Local Volume. Our final sample comprises 39 predominantly isolated hosts with stellar masses $10^{7}<M_\star<10^{10}\,M_\odot$, including 32 hosts searched uniformly in this work and 7 drawn from the literature. We search for satellite candidates within the projected virial radius of each host using $155~\mathrm{deg}^2$ of Legacy Surveys imaging data. We determine satellite membership using surface brightness fluctuation distances from Subaru/HSC, Magellan/IMACS, and Gemini/GMOS imaging, supplemented by literature TRGB distances and radial velocities. From 207 candidates, we confirm 39 satellites with $M_\star>10^5\,M_\odot$ around the 39 hosts. Above our fiducial completeness threshold of $M_\star\gtrsim10^{5.7}\,M_\odot$ and within the projected virial radius, 21 hosts have no confirmed satellites, 10 have one, six have two, and two have four, revealing substantial host-to-host scatter in satellite abundance. Overall, the observed satellite abundances and stellar mass functions are broadly consistent with predictions from the cosmological simulation TNG50 and galaxy formation models calibrated using Milky Way satellites. The projected radial distribution of the satellites is also consistent with theoretical expectations and with satellite populations around Milky Way-mass hosts. In contrast, the quenched fraction of satellites around dwarf hosts is substantially lower than around Milky Way-mass hosts, suggesting that environmental quenching is less efficient in dwarf halos. ELVES-Dwarf provides the first large, homogeneous, distance-confirmed sample of satellites around dwarf hosts and establishes a foundation for understanding galaxy formation and evolution in less-dense environments.

It confirms 39 satellites above M*~10^5 M_sun, revealing large host-to-host scatter in satellite abundance, consistency with TNG50 simulations, and lower quenched fractions in dwarf halos compared to Milky Way-mass hosts.
AI.motivation: To systematically census satellite populations around dwarf galaxy hosts in the Local Volume, filling a gap in our understanding of galaxy formation in less-dense environments where observational data of dwarf satellite systems had been scarce.
AI.method: Survey of 39 isolated dwarf hosts (10^7<M*<10^10 M_sun) using 155 deg^2 of Legacy Surveys imaging, searching satellites within projected virial radii. Membership determined via surface brightness fluctuation distances from Subaru/HSC, Magellan/IMACS, and Gemini/GMOS, supplemented by literature TRGB distances and radial velocities.
AI.result: Confirmed 39 satellites with M*>10^5 M_sun around 39 hosts. Above the completeness threshold of M*~10^5.7 M_sun, host satellite counts ranged from 0 to 4, showing substantial scatter. Satellite abundances and stellar mass functions broadly match TNG50 predictions, but the quenched fraction is substantially lower than around Milky Way-mass hosts.
AI.conclusion: ELVES-Dwarf provides the first large, homogeneous, distance-confirmed sample of satellites around dwarf hosts, establishing a foundation for understanding galaxy formation and evolution in less-dense environments and suggesting that environmental quenching is less efficient in dwarf halos.

title: Statistical analysis of asteroseismic indices and stellar parameters of TESS-observed $δ$ Scuti stars
comment: 17 pages, 18 figures, 3 tables. Published in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: We analyze the statistical properties and asteroseismic indices of delta Scuti stars observed during TESS Cycle 4. Using 2 minute cadence photometry and Fourier analysis, we identified 765 delta Scuti stars in Sectors 40-55, including 179 objects with low-resolution stellar parameters from LAMOST. We examined the distributions of their pulsation and stellar parameters using values from the TESS Input Catalog and LAMOST. Most targets lie within the classical instability strip, follow the period-luminosity relation, and show periods, amplitudes, temperatures, surface gravities, and luminosities consistent with delta Scuti stars. For the LAMOST subsample, we estimated the large frequency separation ($Δν$), $ν_{\rm max}$, and $ν({\rm Amax})$ using an empirical relation and a two-dimensional autocorrelation method. We also derived relations among these asteroseismic indices. This catalog provides a useful sample for future studies of the internal structure and evolution of delta Scuti stars.

The study examines pulsation and stellar parameter distributions and derives asteroseismic indices (Δν, ν_max, ν(Amax)) with empirical relations for a LAMOST subsample, providing a valuable catalog for future internal structure studies.
AI.motivation: To provide a comprehensive catalog of delta Scuti stars from TESS Cycle 4 observations and to characterize their statistical properties and asteroseismic indices, which is important for understanding the internal structure and evolution of these pulsating variable stars.
AI.method: The authors used TESS 2-minute cadence photometry from Sectors 40-55 with Fourier analysis to identify delta Scuti stars. They utilized the TESS Input Catalog for stellar parameters and LAMOST low-resolution spectroscopy for 179 stars. For the LAMOST subsample, they estimated asteroseismic indices (large frequency separation Δν, ν_max, and frequency of maximum amplitude ν(Amax)) using an empirical relation and a two-dimensional autocorrelation method, then derived relations among these indices.

The stars were found to lie within the classical instability strip, follow the period-luminosity relation, and have periods, amplitudes, temperatures, surface gravities, and luminosities consistent with delta Scuti stars. title: Deuteration of Organic Molecules as a Probe of Starless Core and Filament Evolution in Barnard 10
comment: Accepted for publication in PASP. 46 pages, 21 figures
summary: The deuterium fractionation of molecules in starless cores is sensitive to their dynamical histories, which recent magnetohydrodynamical simulations have shown to be extremely varied. The deuterated isotopologues of formaldehyde (H$_2$CO) and methanol (CH$_3$OH) probe deuterium fractionation in simple organic molecules. This complete survey targets 11 low-mass starless cores in the small, quiescent Barnard 10 (B10) region of the Taurus Molecular Cloud. The cores were observed using the 12m Arizona Radio Observatory telescope with a 100% detection rate in transitions of o/pH$_2$CO, HDCO, pD$_2$CO, A/E-CH$_3$OH, and CH$_2$DOH and the dense gas tracer N$_2$H$^+$. The HDCO and pD$_2$CO column densities and deuterium fractions are not correlated with those of the grain-surface deuteration tracer CH$_2$DOH, indicating significant gas-phase formation of deuterated formaldehyde. The observed deuterium fractions do not correlate with evolutionary indicators (e.g. core central density) or physical conditions (e.g. core mass). We also find that cores within the northwestern filament have lower deuterium fractions than cores of similar densities in the other two filaments. These could indicate differential core evolution both between and within entire filaments. Comparing the deuterium fractions of the B10 sample to published sources across different evolutionary stages suggests the inheritance of D$_2$CO from starless cores, although more surveys of organic deuteration are needed to conclusively determine inheritance.

AI.tldr: A complete survey of 11 low-mass starless cores in the Barnard 10 region of Taurus, achieving 100% detection of deuterated formaldehyde and methanol isotopologues plus N2H+. HDCO/pD2CO deuterium fractions do not correlate with CH2DOH (a grain-surface deuteration tracer), indicating significant gas-phase formation of deuterated formaldehyde. Deuteration fractions show no correlation with evolutionary indicators or physical conditions, but cores in the northwestern filament have systematically lower deuterium fractions than similar-density cores in other filaments, suggesting differential core evolution within and between filaments. Comparison with published sources hints at inheritance of D2CO from starless to later stages, though more surveys are needed.
AI.motivation: To characterize deuterium fractionation in simple organic molecules (H2CO and CH3OH) across low-mass starless cores in the quiescent B10 region, linking observed deuteration to the varied dynamical histories predicted by recent MHD simulations of core formation and evolution.
AI.method: Complete survey using the 12m Arizona Radio Observatory telescope of 11 low-mass starless cores in Barnard 10 (Taurus Molecular Cloud), observing transitions of o/pH2CO, HDCO, pD2CO, A/E-CH3OH, CH2DOH, and N2H+. Column densities and deuterium fractions were derived and analyzed against evolutionary indicators (e.g., central density), physical conditions (core mass), filament subdivision, and compared to published sources across evolutionary stages.
AI.result: 100% detection rate across all target species in all 11 cores. HDCO/pD2CO deuterium fractions are uncorrelated with CH2DOH deuteration, pointing to significant gas-phase deuteration of formaldehyde that decouples it from grain-surface chemistry. No correlations with evolutionary indicators or physical conditions are found. Cores in the northwestern filament show systematically lower deuterium fractions than cores of similar density in the other two filaments. Inter-source comparison suggests D2CO inheritance from starless cores to later stages.
AI.conclusion: Differential deuteration between and within filaments implies varied core dynamical histories as anticipated by simulations. Gas-phase processes contribute to deuterated formaldehyde formation independently of grain-surface deuterated methanol. The possible inheritance of D2CO suggests chemical memory across evolutionary stages, but broader surveys of organic deuteration are required for a conclusive determination.

title: TESS Observations of Seven Newly Identified High-amplitude $δ$ Scuti Stars
comment: 13 pages, 11 figures, 8 tables. Published in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: We report seven newly identified high-amplitude $δ$ Scuti (HADS) stars. Among them, two stars (TIC 30977864 and TIC 387379145) exhibit pure radial pulsation without the excitation of non-radial modes. TIC 30977864 is classified as a double-mode HADS star, while the other four stars potentially show triple-mode HADS behavior. TIC 112682462 and TIC 255603395 closely resemble RR Lyrae stars based on their light curves, position in the period-luminosity diagram, and the period-ratio diagram. However, without spectral observations, it is challenging to ascertain whether these two stars are HADS or RR Lyrae stars. TIC 281695001 exhibits a fundamental frequency amplitude smaller than that of the first overtone, suggesting the presence of intriguing phenomena that necessitate further analysis. We analyzed the relationship between metallicity and period using data provided by Netzel & Smolec. The metallicities of the 176 stars display a broad distribution ranging from -2.0 dex to 0.5 dex, with periods spanning 0.05 to 0.20 days. This random distribution of metallicities may contribute to the dispersion observed in the $P_1/P_0$ ratio. To derive more accurate conclusions, future spectroscopic observations of a larger sample of HADS stars are crucial. These observations will provide precise rotational velocities and more accurate determinations of metallicities.

AI.tldr: The paper reports the identification of seven new high-amplitude δ Scuti (HADS) stars. Two show pure radial pulsation (single-mode), one is a double-mode HADS, and four potentially exhibit triple-mode HADS behavior. Two stars (TIC 112682462 and TIC 255603395) closely resemble RR Lyrae stars based on light curves and period-luminosity/period-ratio diagrams, but lack spectral confirmation. One star (TIC 281695001) shows an inverted amplitude ratio (first overtone stronger than fundamental), warranting further study. Metallicity-period analysis of 176 stars from Netzel & Smolec shows a broad metallicity distribution (-2.0 to 0.5 dex) with periods of 0.05-0.20 days, possibly contributing to scatter in the P1/P0 ratio. Future spectroscopic observations of a larger sample are needed for accurate rotational velocities and metallicities.
AI.motivation: To identify and characterize new high-amplitude δ Scuti (HADS) stars, especially those showing pure radial pulsation modes (double- and triple-mode behavior), and to investigate the relationship between metallicity and pulsation period to better understand dispersion in period ratios.
AI.method: Analysis of photometric data (presumably from TESS/TIC) to identify HADS stars via light curves, pulsation frequency analysis, and classification using period-luminosity and period-ratio diagrams. Metallicity-period relationships were examined using existing data from Netzel & Smolec from 176 stars.
AI.result: Seven new HADS stars identified: two with pure radial pulsation (TIC 30977864 double-mode; TIC 387379145 single-mode/radial only), four potentially triple-mode HADS, and one (TIC 281695001) with fundamental amplitude smaller than first overtone. Two stars ambiguously classified between HADS and RR Lyrae. Metallicity distribution of the 176-star sample spans -2.0 to 0.5 dex with periods 0.05-0.20 days, showing a random distribution that may contribute to P1/P0 scatter.
AI.conclusion: The identification of new multi-mode HADS stars expands the known sample of these valuable asteroseismic targets. The ambiguous HADS/RR Lyrae classifications and the anomalous amplitude ratio in TIC 281695001 highlight the need for spectroscopic follow-up. Future observations with larger samples and precise measurements of rotational velocities and metallicities are essential for more robust conclusions.

title: Formation of Heavy Seed Black Holes and Little Red Dots-like Compact Clusters in Metal-enriched Star-forming Regions
comment: 19 pages, 13 figures
summary: The origin of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) in the early Universe remains uncertain. While the classical direct-collapse scenario requires pristine gas exposed to intense Lyman-Werner (LW) radiation, recent JWST observations suggest that early growing BHs may reside in compact, metal-enriched environments. We investigate early BH formation using a cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic simulation that self-consistently follows the formation and evolution of rapidly accreting supermassive stars (SMSs). We find that intense LW radiation develops in clustered star-forming regions; by the time the first heavy seed forms, the mass-weighted internal intensity has reached $J_{21}\sim1000$. Most seeds form in weakly metal-enriched gas with [Z/H]$\sim-3$ to $-2$, because the strongest LW fields occur in regions already enriched by previous stellar feedback. All halos above $10^9M_\odot$ in our zoom-in region host a BH more massive than $10^5M_\odot$. We construct stellar spectra using MIST/PHOENIX libraries for normal stars and $6000~\mathrm{K}$ blackbody spectra for bloated SMSs. Five of eight massive clusters with stellar masses larger than $10^6~M_\odot$ exhibit intrinsically V-shaped spectra similar to those of Little Red Dots (LRDs). In the most prominent cases, luminous SMSs dominate the red optical emission, although Balmer breaks in normal stellar populations also contribute. We also identify off-center LRD-like systems in our simulation resembling those recently reported in strongly lensed observations. Our results suggest that heavy-seed formation, compact-cluster formation, and LRD-like continuum emission are linked outcomes of clustered, weakly metal-enriched, strongly irradiated environments.

AI.tldr: Using a cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic simulation that self-consistently tracks supermassive star (SMS) formation, the authors find that supermassive black hole seeds form in weakly metal-enriched ([Z/H]~-3 to -2) gas bathed in intense Lyman-Werner radiation (J21~1000) produced by clustered star formation. All >10^9 Msun halos host >10^5 Msun BHs, and five of eight massive clusters exhibit V-shaped spectra resembling Little Red Dots (LRDs), linking heavy-seed formation to compact-cluster formation and LRD-like emission.
AI.motivation: The origin of supermassive black holes in the early Universe remains uncertain. Classical direct-collapse scenarios require pristine gas under intense Lyman-Werner radiation, but new JWST observations suggest early growing BHs may live in compact, metal-enriched environments, motivating a re-examination of BH formation pathways that can reconcile theory with observations.
AI.method: The authors run a cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic simulation that self-consistently follows the formation and evolution of rapidly accreting supermassive stars. They track mass-weighted internal Lyman-Werner intensity, metallicity of seed-forming gas, and halo BH occupation. They construct stellar spectra using MIST/PHOENIX libraries for normal stars and 6000 K blackbodies for bloated SMSs to compare continuum shapes with Little Red Dot observations.
AI.result: Intense LW radiation (J21~1000) develops in clustered star-forming regions by the time the first heavy seed forms. Most seeds form in weakly metal-enriched gas at [Z/H]~-3 to -2 because the strongest LW fields arise in previously enriched regions. All halos above 10^9 Msun host BHs more massive than 10^5 Msun. Five of eight massive clusters (>10^6 Msun) show intrinsically V-shaped spectra similar to LRDs, with luminous SMSs dominating red optical emission and Balmer breaks contributing. Off-center LRD-like systems resembling strongly lensed detections are also identified.
AI.conclusion: Heavy-seed formation, compact-cluster formation, and LRD-like continuum emission are linked outcomes of clustered, weakly metal-enriched, strongly irradiated environments in the early Universe. This suggests a unified pathway connecting SMBH seeds to observed JWST spectral features.

title: A Data-Driven Model for $r$-Process Production Patterns
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal (ApJ), 48 pages
summary: Using the elemental abundances in 68 metal-poor (MP) stars, we present a data-driven model for $r$-process production patterns covering Sr to U. We show that essentially all the $r$-process patterns in those and other test stars can be adequately explained as mixtures of Patterns 1 and 2, which provides theoretical insights into the empirical categories of limited-$r$, $r$-I, and $r$-II stars. We carry out an extensive survey of the yield templates produced by parametric $r$-process calculations. We propose that Pattern 2 may be dominated by a single template and points to regularity in $r$-process production by a subset of neutron star mergers (NSMs), while Pattern 1 is the average superposition of multiple templates and reflects production by other NSMs and perhaps also some magneto-rotational supernovae. We raise possible systematic issues with abundance ratios for elements measured in different ionization states, and highlight the need for examining the Os, Ir, and Pt measurements for HD~122563, which is dominated by Pattern 1 with a prominent Pt peak in our model. If this result is confirmed, the meaning of the limited-$r$ category requires drastic revision. Further measurements of a wider range of $r$-process elements in a larger sample of MP stars are critical to test and improve our model.

AI.tldr: A data-driven model using elemental abundances from 68 metal-poor stars shows that essentially all r-process production patterns from Sr to U can be explained as mixtures of two components (Patterns 1 and 2), with implications for the empirical categories of limited-r, r-I, and r-II stars, and pointing to different astrophysical sources for each pattern.
AI.motivation: To understand the origins and diversity of r-process element production by building a data-driven model that can categorize and explain observed abundance patterns in metal-poor stars, and to link these empirical categories to physical production mechanisms.
AI.method: Analyzes elemental abundances from 68 metal-poor stars to build a data-driven model of r-process patterns spanning Sr to U, then compares against parametric r-process yield templates from an extensive survey of calculations.
AI.result: All r-process patterns can be explained as mixtures of two patterns. Pattern 2 appears dominated by a single template, suggesting regularity from a subset of neutron star mergers, while Pattern 1 is an average superposition of multiple templates, reflecting contributions from other NSMs and possibly magneto-rotational supernovae.
AI.conclusion: The two-component model provides theoretical insight into empirical r-process star categories and raises questions about potential systematic issues in abundance measurements, particularly for specific elements like Os, Ir, Pt in certain stars. Further measurements in larger samples are needed to test and refine the model.

title: Detection of a triple nucleus in the Wolf-Rayet composite Sy 2 galaxy NGC 6764
comment: 3 pages, 1 figure, accepted in RNAAS
summary:
We report adaptive-optics Ks-band imaging of the composite Seyfert 2 and Wolf-Rayet galaxy NGC 6764 (D = 32 Mpc), obtained with LUCI/SOUL at the Large Binocular Telescope. The nucleus resolves into three compact sources with pairwise projected separations of 0.07-0.20 arcsec, corresponding to 11.0-30.9 pc.
  All three have indistinguishable H, Ks, H2, and Br-gamma colours, so photometry alone cannot separate accretion from star formation. The system is consistent with a Seyfert nucleus and two star-forming regions, but a dual or triple AGN cannot be excluded. In the latter case, the separations would be two orders of magnitude smaller than in any confirmed or candidate AGN triplet reported to date. Diffraction-limited near-infrared integral-field spectroscopy is required to establish the nature of each component.

AI.tldr: Adaptive-optics Ks-band imaging of NGC 6764 (a Seyfert 2 and Wolf-Rayet galaxy) resolves the nucleus into three compact sources separated by 11-31 pc. All three have identical colors, so photometry cannot distinguish an AGN from star formation. The system may be a Seyfert nucleus with two starbursts, or a remarkably compact triple AGN—two orders of magnitude closer than any previously reported AGN triplet. Diffraction-limited near-infrared IFU spectroscopy is needed to determine the nature of each component.
AI.motivation: To resolve the composite nucleus of NGC 6764 at high spatial resolution and determine whether the three compact sources represent a Seyfert nucleus plus star-forming regions or a potential (very compact) multiple AGN system, which would be unprecedented.
AI.method: Adaptive-optics Ks-band imaging obtained with the LUCI/SOUL instrument at the Large Binocular Telescope, resolving and analyzing the photometric colors (H, Ks, H2, Br-gamma) of three compact nuclear sources.
AI.result: The nucleus resolves into three compact sources with separations of 0.07-0.20 arcsec (11.0-30.9 pc). All three sources have indistinguishable H, Ks, H2, and Br-gamma colors, preventing photometric discrimination between accretion and star formation. The data are consistent both with a Seyfert nucleus plus two star-forming regions and with a dual/triple AGN scenario; the latter would be two orders of magnitude more compact than any known AGN triplet.
AI.conclusion: Photometry alone cannot establish the nature of the three components. Diffraction-limited near-infrared integral-field spectroscopy is required to definitively identify each source.

title: Direct Measurement of Polar Coronal Hole-like Solar Wind in its Acceleration Phase
comment: 21 pages, 4 figures, Under Review in ApJL, Comments Welcome
summary: The early evolution of fast polar coronal hole (PCH) solar wind remains largely unconstrained by in situ measurements. In March 2025, Parker Solar Probe (Parker) at its closest approach of 9.86 Solar Radii ($R_\odot$) measured outflow from a large equatorial coronal hole (ECH) which was also measured at 1\,au and at intermediate distances by Solar Orbiter (also near its perihelion). At 1\,au the stream properties are consistent with PCH properties established by Ulysses. The stream was measured by Parker substantially below the Alfvén surface, with proton temperatures in excess of 2\,MK and a speed at $\sim$10\,$R_\odot$ which was only $\sim$60\% of its asymptotic value. The Solar Orbiter data indicates that the acceleration is largely complete by 60~$R_{\odot}$. Spherically-polarized fluctuations in the stream are observed to develop from near-transverse and small-angle at Parker to full reversal ``switchbacks'' at Solar Orbiter. Comparison of the implied acceleration profile to historical doppler-dimming measurements suggests that the stream's low coronal acceleration is similar to that of PCH flows. Consistent with previous work, this acceleration requires significantly more energy than can be provided by the observed thermal pressure gradients, with a significant contribution likely from the abundant Alfvénic fluctuation energy observed at Parker. These observations provide unique constraints on models of the radial evolution of the fastest solar wind, and indicate that these wind streams experience gradual, steady acceleration over their first few tens of solar radii of evolution.

AI.tldr: Using the rare alignment of Parker Solar Probe (9.86 R_sun), Solar Orbiter (~60 R_sun), and 1 au spacecraft in March 2025, the paper constrains the early radial evolution of fast polar coronal hole solar wind, showing gradual acceleration over the first tens of solar radii, with proton temperatures >2 MK and Alfvénic fluctuation development into switchbacks.
AI.motivation: The early evolution of fast polar coronal hole solar wind has remained largely unconstrained due to the lack of in situ measurements close to the Sun. A rare quadrature configuration of multiple spacecraft measuring the same equatorial coronal hole stream provides a unique opportunity to constrain this evolution.
AI.method: The study combines in situ measurements from Parker Solar Probe at ~10 R_sun (below the Alfvén surface), Solar Orbiter at intermediate distances (~60 R_sun), and 1 au observations, comparing the stream properties, acceleration profiles, and fluctuation characteristics (spherically-polarized Alfvénic fluctuations transitioning to switchbacks) across the radial range, and comparing to historical doppler-dimming measurements.
