AI.conclusion: A multi-survey approach using only standard survey products provides a powerful method to characterise large numbers of supernovae that would otherwise be lost. This technique will be essential for maximising scientific return from current and future surveys including GOTO, BlackGEM, Vera C. Rubin Observatory's LSST, and GOTTA.

title: Irreducible-Mass Growth and Extractable Energy in a Self-Gravitating Blandford-Znajek Engine
comment: 5 pages, no figures
summary: Wang recently constructed a self-gravitating split-monopole Blandford-Znajek engine and obtained its secular horizon mass and angular-momentum loss rates. We determine the previously unknown consequences of this evolution: the growth of the irreducible mass, the division of rotational work between outgoing electromagnetic power and horizon dissipation, and the lifetime-integrated energy removed from the horizon. For fixed magnetic flux and impedance matching, one half of the instantaneous rotational work is carried outward, and one half irreversibly increases the horizon area. Integrating Wang's spin-down trajectory, we find in the weak-field limit the exact results A_f/A_0=\sqrt{e} and E_{extr}^H/(M_{H,0}c^2)=1-exp{1/4}/\sqrt{2}\simeq 0.09206. The leading maximum-power spin-flux allocation instead gives E_{\rm extr}^{H}/(M_{H,0}c^2)\simeq 0.04668. These results provide the first irreducible-mass and extractable-energy accounting of Wang's engine. Their extension from quasilocal horizon quantities to energy received at infinity requires a separate flux analysis.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the evolutionary consequences of Wang's self-gravitating split-monopole Blandford-Znajek engine, determining the growth of irreducible mass, the division of rotational work between outgoing electromagnetic power and horizon dissipation, and lifetime-integrated energy extraction. Exact results are derived in the weak-field limit: A_f/A_0=√e and E_extr^H/(M_H,0 c^2)≈0.09206, with a lower bound of ≈0.04668 for maximum-power spin-flux allocation.
AI.motivation: Wang previously constructed a self-gravitating split-monopole Blandford-Znajek engine and computed its secular horizon mass and angular-momentum loss rates. However, the consequences of this evolution—specifically the growth of irreducible mass and the division of rotational work between outgoing electromagnetic power and horizon dissipation—were previously unknown. This work aims to provide the first accounting of these quantities.
AI.method: The authors analyze Wang's spin-down trajectory of a self-gravitating split-monopole Blandford-Znajek engine. They integrate the spin-down dynamics to compute instantaneous and lifetime-integrated quantities, including the irreducible mass growth and energy extraction from the horizon. Exact analytical results are obtained in the weak-field limit, and a maximum-power spin-flux allocation case is also considered.
AI.result: For fixed magnetic flux and impedance matching, half of the instantaneous rotational work is carried outward while the other half irreversibly increases the horizon area. In the weak-field limit, exact results are A_f/A_0=√e and E_extr^H/(M_H,0 c^2)=1-exp(1/4)/√2≈0.09206. The maximum-power spin-flux allocation yields E_extr^H/(M_H,0 c^2)≈0.04668. The authors note that extension from quasilocal horizon quantities to energy received at infinity requires a separate flux analysis, indicating future work needed for a complete astrophysical interpretation.

title: Integrated Mass Loss for Very Metal-poor Stars: Asterosesimic Red Giant Masses of K2 Globular Cluster NGC 5897
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJL, 16 pages, 10 figures, 2 tables
summary: Mass loss in low-mass stars during the red giant branch (RGB) and early asymptotic giant branch (EAGB) phases plays a key role in shaping stellar evolution, yet its dependence on stellar parameters such as metallicity remains poorly constrained, with observational studies yielding conflicting trends. We present the first asteroseismic analysis of RGB and EAGB stars in NGC 5897, the most distant and metal-poor globular cluster observed by the Kepler space telescope during the K2 mission. We detected solar-like oscillations and derived the frequency of maximum power excess, $ν_{\rm max}$, for 20 RGB and 6 EAGB stars. Using asteroseismic scaling relations, we derived mean masses of $\overline{M}_{\rm RGB} = 0.74\pm0.01\,M_{\odot}$ and $\overline{M}_{\rm EAGB}=0.65\pm 0.03\,M_{\odot}$. The inferred integrated mass loss between the two phases is $ΔM_{\rm RGB-EAGB}=0.08\pm 0.03 \,M_{\odot}$. We present an updated mass-loss--metallicity relation for Type I globular clusters, extending it to the very metal-poor regime and supporting decreasing integrated RGB mass loss with decreasing metallicity.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first asteroseismic analysis of red giant branch (RGB) and early asymptotic giant branch (EAGB) stars in NGC 5897, the most distant and metal-poor globular cluster observed by Kepler/K2. Using scaling relations from detected solar-like oscillations, the authors derive mean masses of 0.74 M☉ for RGB and 0.65 M☉ for EAGB stars, yielding an integrated mass loss of 0.08 M☉ between phases. They present an updated mass-loss–metallicity relation supporting decreasing integrated RGB mass loss with decreasing metallicity.
AI.motivation: Mass loss during the RGB and EAGB phases is crucial for stellar evolution modeling but its dependence on parameters like metallicity is poorly constrained, with conflicting results from different observational studies.
AI.method: Asteroseismic analysis of solar-like oscillations in RGB and EAGB stars of NGC 5897 using Kepler K2 data; detection of ν_max and application of asteroseismic scaling relations to derive stellar masses and integrated mass loss.
AI.result: Detected oscillations in 20 RGB and 6 EAGB stars; mean masses of 0.74±0.01 M☉ (RGB) and 0.65±0.03 M☉ (EAGB); integrated RGB-to-EAGB mass loss of 0.08±0.03 M☉; updated mass-loss–metallicity relation extended to the very metal-poor regime.
AI.conclusion: The results support decreasing integrated RGB mass loss with decreasing metallicity, extending and refining the mass-loss–metallicity relation for Type I globular clusters to the very metal-poor regime.

title: The JWST Emission Line Survey (JELS): A narrow-band determination of the H$α$ Luminosity Function and Cosmic Star Formation into the Epoch of Reionization
comment: 21 pages, 8 figures, submitted to the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (MNRAS)
summary: The recent star-formation activity in galaxies can be optimally traced by the H$α$ emission line, with the resulting H$α$ luminosity function (LF) at a given epoch providing a reliable probe of cosmic star formation. We present the first narrow-band determined H$α$ LF into the Epoch of Reionization (EoR) at $z\sim6.1$, using 39 H$α$ emitters selected from the JWST Emission Line Survey (JELS). The observed and dust-corrected LFs are broadly consistent with recent slitless spectroscopic measurements but show notable discrepancies with predictions from cosmological simulations, likely reflecting differences in emission-line and dust modelling. Fits combining multiple LF datasets help constrain the high-redshift faint-end slope of the H$α$ LF ($-1.79<α_{\rm{Hα}}<-1.62$), but there remains uncertainty in its evolution with redshift. Integrating the JELS dust-corrected H$α$ LFs yields a star-formation rate density of $\log_{10}(ρ_{\rm{SFR_{Hα}}}\,/\,\rm{M_{\odot}\,yr^{-1}\,Mpc^{-3}})=-1.93\,^{+0.14}_{-0.12}$ or $-2.00\,^{+0.16}_{-0.10}$, assuming a continuum-to-line extinction ratios $η_{\rm{dust}}=A_{\rm{cont}}(\rm{6563\,\mathring{A}})/A_{\rm{Hα}}=1$ and 0.44, respectively. Both measurements are consistent within uncertainties with previous results using standard assumptions for the LF integration limit ($L_{\rm{Hα,\,lim}}$) and SFR calibration constant $κ_{\rm{Hα}}$, despite the uncertainties in the dust corrections. We explore the metallicity dependence of $κ_{\rm{Hα}}$ and find $ρ_{\rm{SFR_{Hα}}}$ decreases 0.43 dex compared to the fiducial result and is no longer consistent with UV-determined $ρ_{\rm{SFR}}$ at $z\sim6$. This work highlights the importance of narrow-band surveys in probing the faint H$α$ population and providing new constraints on cosmic star-formation activity into the EoR.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first narrow-band observed Hα luminosity function at z~6.1 (into the Epoch of Reionization) from 39 Hα emitters in the JWST Emission Line Survey (JELS), finding results broadly consistent with slitless spectroscopic measurements but discrepant with cosmological simulations. Dust-corrected star-formation rate densities are log10(ρSFR) ≈ -1.93 to -2.00, consistent with previous results under standard assumptions, though metallicity-dependent SFR calibrations reduce this by 0.43 dex.
AI.motivation: To trace recent star-formation activity into the Epoch of Reionization (z~6) using narrow-band Hα observations, which are an optimal tracer of instantaneous star formation and provide a reliable probe of cosmic star formation through the Hα luminosity function. This work provides the first narrow-band determined Hα LF at z~6.1, filling a gap where slitless spectroscopy and simulations yield differing predictions.
AI.method: The authors selected 39 Hα emitters from the JWST Emission Line Survey (JELS) using narrow-band imaging to construct the Hα luminosity function at z~6.1. They measured observed and dust-corrected LFs, fitted multiple LF datasets together to constrain the faint-end slope, and integrated the dust-corrected LFs to derive the star-formation rate density under different extinction ratio assumptions (ηdust=1 and 0.44). They also explored the metallicity dependence of the SFR calibration constant κHα.
AI.result: The observed and dust-corrected LFs are broadly consistent with slitless spectroscopic measurements but show discrepancies with cosmological simulation predictions. Multi-dataset fits constrain the faint-end slope to -1.79<αHα<-1.62 with uncertain redshift evolution. The dust-corrected star-formation rate density is log10(ρSFR/M⊙yr⁻¹Mpc⁻³) = -1.93(+0.14/-0.12) or -2.00(+0.16/-0.10) for ηdust=1 and 0.44. Both are consistent with previous results. Accounting for metallicity dependence in κHα decreases ρSFRHα by 0.43 dex, making it inconsistent with UV-determined ρSFR at z~6.
AI.conclusion: This work demonstrates the importance of narrow-band surveys for probing the faint Hα population and constraining cosmic star-formation activity into the Epoch of Reionization. While results align with existing measurements under standard assumptions, the discrepancies with simulations and the significant impact of metallicity-dependent SFR calibrations highlight remaining uncertainties in dust and emission-line modelling at high redshift.

title: A wavelet-based model of magnetic turbulence over a Parker spiral field
summary:
The propagation of Solar Energetic Particles (SEPs) through the heliosphere is strongly influenced by solar-wind magnetic turbulence, which governs particle scattering, field-line wandering, and cross-field transport. These processes shape SEP intensity profiles, anisotropies, and arrival times. Because heliospheric turbulence spans a vast range of scales, direct numerical simulations cannot capture its full spectrum. title: The quiescent states of V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr: VLT/X-shooter and Swift/XRT+UVOT observations

summary: Symbiotic recurrent novae are symbiotic binaries in which multiple thermonuclear outbursts have been observed. Only four such systems are currently known in the Galaxy: T CrB, RS Oph, V745 Sco, and V3890 Sgr. They provide convenient laboratories for studying accretion and binary interaction in symbiotic novae during quiescence. We characterise the quiescent states of the less-studied systems V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr and compare their properties with those of T CrB and RS Oph. We analyse VLT/X-shooter spectra together with Swift/XRT and UVOT observations, supplemented by ground-based optical photometry and archival data. We determine the spectral types of the red-giant donors and compare the spectral energy distributions of the systems with those of single bulge giants of the same spectral type to investigate the properties of the accretion. We classify the donor stars in V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr as M7III and M6.5III, respectively. We derive reddenings and distances consistent with both systems belonging to the Galactic bulge. Both objects exhibit a significant ultraviolet excess relative to normal late-type giants, indicating ongoing accretion during quiescence. From this excess we estimate mass transfer rates of the order of $\sim 5 \times 10^{-8}\ M_{\odot}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, broadly consistent with the observed recurrence timescales. These results suggest that recurrent nova eruptions in V745 Sco and V3890 Sgr can be sustained by long-term accretion at approximately the present rate, without requiring an episode of enhanced accretion similar to that observed in T CrB.
